name: Auricula Felis Modification
description: Restructures the human pinna into feline-form ears positioned higher on the skull, complete with independent muscular control allowing the ears to rotate, flatten, and perk. The modification replaces the original ear structure entirely — this is not ears on top of ears, it's a full auricular rebuild. The ears are covered in short fur with color options matching or contrasting the user's hair. They provide mildly enhanced directional hearing as a functional bonus. Cat ears are the single most popular radical cosmetic modification in Meridian 88, cutting across all tiers and demographics. In the Shelf, cat-eared residents outnumber unmodified-eared residents in some blocks. The ears move expressively — they flatten when the user is annoyed, perk when interested, and swivel toward sounds automatically — which makes them functionally an emotional broadcast system. Some users love this. Some learn to consciously control the ear movements to mask their feelings. Some never bother.
source_organism: Felis catus (domestic cat), Caracal caracal (caracal, tufted variant)
manufacturer: Helix Biosystems (standard), Lacuna Genomics (luxury tufted variants)
procedure: Auricular cartilage dissolution and regrowth with retroviral reshaping, 1 session under local anesthetic
expression_time: 6–8 weeks for full cartilage restructuring and fur growth
reversibility: Reversible with second cartilage regrowth session; leaves slight scarring at ear margins
side_effects: Ears are hypersensitive to touch for first 2 months
Involuntary ear movement broadcasts emotional state
Budget installations sometimes produce asymmetric ears
social_perception: Mainstream to the point of unremarkability. Cat ears are the default cosmetic mod. Not having them is more of a statement than having them. Children born to two cat-eared parents sometimes express the trait partially.
story_hooks: A spy's cover is blown because their cat ears flatten involuntarily during a lie — the person they're deceiving reads ears better than words
A gene clinic's cat-ear package is contaminated with feline behavioral sequences, causing a neighborhood of recipients to develop territorial aggression
